# PLAN — iteration 1

## Current state assessment

The incumbent is timing-feasible at 0.554 ns setup WNS and 0.098 ns hold WHS, with 41 LUTs, 90 FFs, no DSPs or BRAMs, and a passing frozen testbench. The objective is strictly fewer LUTs once all gates pass. The editable top is only a wrapper, so this iteration can replace its arbiter instance with equivalent top-level logic while leaving the frozen register file intact. Top numeric latency is unknown; do not add an annotation based on the typed child latencies.

## Hypothesis

Replacing the arbiter’s modulo-based cyclic search and variable-index request lookup with fixed priority cases may reduce LUT use while preserving the registered grant and write-channel behavior.

## Instruction for generator

In `rr_regfile`, replace the `rr_arbiter4` instance with top-level arbiter logic that uses `last` and explicit cases for the four cyclic requester orders; avoid modulo arithmetic, integer loop indices, and variable-index reads of `req`. Keep the existing registered grant, write-enable, address, and data behavior, including reset to `last=3`, zero outputs when no request is present, and unchanged `last` on idle cycles. Continue connecting the registered write channel to the frozen `regfile8x8` instance so its read-first behavior and cycle timing remain intact. Preserve the interface and clock, and do not add a top latency annotation.
